svg.title: Two ways molecules cross a membrane
svg.desc: (a) A semipermeable membrane drawn as a column of blocks separated by narrow gaps, the pores. Molecules of many sizes lie on both sides. Only the smallest fit through the pores: one small molecule passes right and another passes left, while the large molecules stay where they are. (b) Molecules packed closely on both sides of a solid membrane. A few of them have dissolved in the membrane and are diffusing across it.
